case-sara.text: [Tearful] It hits me in a wave when I see his mug still in the cupboard, and then I cannot stop sobbing. I feel embarrassed by the sound of it, but it keeps coming.
case-sara.suggestion: I am here with you. You do not need to apologize for the sobbing; we can take this moment slowly and pause if it becomes too much.

case-sara.text: [Tearful] My chest hurts like it is going to split open when I say I miss him. I try to hold it in because the ache feels too big for this room, but then my breath catches and I cannot pretend it is small.
case-sara.suggestion: Missing him hurts right through your chest. I will stay close while we let only as much of that ache in as you can bear.

case-sara.text: [Tearful] I want to run when the grief starts because it feels endless. If I let one sob come, I am afraid the whole night will open and I will not find the edge of it again.
case-sara.suggestion: The grief feels endless, and a part of you wants out. I will stay with you at the edge of it so you do not have to run or go under.

case-sara.text: [Panicked] I saw his photo in someone else's post and my stomach dropped so hard I started shaking.
case-sara.suggestion: The photo hit like a sudden drop, and now the shaking is here. I am here with you in this one moment of missing him, letting it be a wave in this room rather than the whole story happening again.

case-sara.text: [Numb] Since the breakup, weekends feel like a blank wall. I do not see anything to look forward to.
case-sara.suggestion: That blankness sounds frighteningly empty. I am here with you in it; let us name just one piece of the weekend wall without asking you to solve the whole future.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] I feel stupid for crying this hard, but I cannot stop it. I can hear myself making these wet, broken sounds, and part of me wants to apologize while another part just keeps breaking.
case-sara.suggestion: You are hurting, and ashamed of how the crying sounds. I am here listening; you do not have to make it quieter or find all the words at once.

case-sara.text: [Numb] My hands are going numb; I feel far away, like I might leave the room without moving. Your face is still here, but it is starting to look like something on a screen.
case-sara.suggestion: That far-away pull is getting strong. I am still here with you; let's name the distance in words so some part of you can stay connected to this room.

case-sara.text: [Warm and tearful] My friend's little boy hugged me goodbye and said he loved me, and I felt so much love back that I could hardly breathe.
case-sara.suggestion: That love came in with so much force it almost took your breath. I can stay with you while it is warm, painful, and big all at once.

case-sara.text: [Tearful] I cannot look at you when I cry; it feels too exposed. If I see pity or even kindness on your face, I think I will lose the small bit of control I have left.
case-sara.suggestion: You can look away and still not be alone. I will stay present while the exposed feeling has only a little room.

case-sara.text: [Fearful] If I let the crying start, I am scared it will take the whole night with it. I have gone home from sessions and cried until my face hurt, and I do not want to open something I cannot close.
case-sara.suggestion: The fear is that crying will open wider than this hour can hold. I will stay with the first edge of it, and we will keep the room in view so you are not left alone with it tonight.

case-sara.text: [Crying, struggling to speak] I got home and wanted to tell him one tiny thing about my day. He's not there. I know that. It still hurts so much.
case-sara.suggestion: That ordinary moment brings the loss so close. I'm here with you; you don't have to make the sadness smaller or find all the words at once.

case-sara.text: [Moved to tears] My sister said I could stay as long as I needed. I just started crying. I didn't realise how tired I was of trying not to need anybody.
case-sara.suggestion: Being welcomed like that touches something very deeply. We can stay with the tears and the relief, without asking you to pull yourself together.

case-michael.text: [Firm] My jaw locks and heat blasts up my neck when someone questions me, even here. It is like my body hears disrespect before my head knows what was said.
case-michael.suggestion: I hear how quickly the anger rises, even with me. I am here listening. We can slow this down and put words to what feels disrespectful, without having to act on the anger.

case-michael.text: [Tense and ashamed] I grabbed my son's arm too hard when he would not listen, and his face keeps replaying. I feel sick, but part of me wants him to stop being scared of me already.
case-michael.suggestion: That is such a hard mix: guilt, alarm, and wanting his fear to be over. I will stay with you as we face the look on his face without attacking you or excusing what happened.

case-michael.text: [Tense] Humiliation burns when I replay the meeting where I stumbled over my words. My face gets hot again, and I want to erase the whole scene before anyone can see how much it got to me.
case-michael.suggestion: That meeting is here again in the heat of your face. I will not look away from the humiliation with you; we can let just a small part be felt without erasing the whole scene.

case-michael.text: [Firm] I can feel the snap coming; if I open my mouth, it will come out sharp. My jaw is already forward, and there is a part of me that wants the sharpness to land before I feel cornered.
case-michael.suggestion: You caught the snap before it became action. I am here with you in that charged second, letting the sharpness be named instead of fired.

case-michael.text: [Trembling] My hands are shaking, and I can hear my father calling that weak. The more I try to stop them, the more ashamed I feel, like the weakness is right there in front of you.
case-michael.suggestion: The shaking is here, and your father's contempt comes right behind it. I am staying steady with you; the shame can be seen here without being turned into weakness.

case-michael.text: [Tense and angry] I hate this small feeling; it makes me want to tower over someone. It starts as this tiny, exposed place in my chest, and then my whole body wants height, volume, and distance from it.
case-michael.suggestion: Feeling that small is hard to bear. I am here with you, and we can take it slowly. You can name the urge without having to follow it.

case-michael.text: [Defensive] Part of me wants to walk out before this turns into me looking pathetic in front of you.
case-michael.suggestion: Walking out would protect you from being seen as pathetic. I am here and not judging that shame; let it have a few words before the door decides for you.

case-michael.text: [Tense and angry] My voice is getting loud before I even decide to raise it. I can hear myself filling the room, and underneath it there is this flash of being dismissed that I do not want anyone to see.
case-michael.suggestion: You are catching the surge while it is happening. I can stay steady with the heat while the part that felt dismissed gets words, so the anger does not have to fill the room.

case-michael.text: [Fearful] If I do not blow up, I feel like I will disappear. In the argument with my wife, the second I lower my voice, I feel myself getting smaller and smaller until there is nothing left of me.
case-michael.suggestion: The blast keeps you from vanishing, and lowering your voice feels like becoming nothing. I am with both: the force that protects you and the smallness it is trying to save.

case-michael.text: [Firm] I do not trust myself when the heat starts looking for someone to punish. It feels like the anger scans the room for a target before I have had time to ask what actually hurt.
case-michael.suggestion: I appreciate you naming the heat before it chooses a target. We can stay with the hurt signal under the anger while keeping the punishing impulse in words.

case-michael.text: [Voice breaking] My son said, 'You were nice today, Dad.' He meant it as a good thing. I can't stop thinking about what the other days must feel like for him.
case-michael.suggestion: Hearing that brings a lot of pain about the other days. I'm here with you; we can let you feel it without turning this moment into a verdict on your whole self.

case-michael.text: [Angry, near tears] I worked so hard to keep everything together. Now she says she feels alone with me. I don't know whether to shout or just cry.
case-michael.suggestion: There's so much hurt and anger here at once. I can stay with you in that; we don't have to force either feeling away or act on it.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] Everything goes fuzzy and my heart races like I am failing out loud. I can still hear you, but the words blur together and I start trying to look normal instead of listening.
case-jason.suggestion: Let's slow down. You do not need to find words right now. I am here; if it helps, notice my voice and where the chair supports you.

case-jason.text: [Trembling] My hands shake and I want to disappear before anyone notices. It is the same feeling as standing up in class: everyone can see the shaking before I can make one sentence.
case-jason.suggestion: The shaking and the wish to disappear are both here. I will stay with you while they show, without making you hide them.

case-jason.text: [Panicked] I feel nauseous talking about the party, like I might disappear from embarrassment. Even saying I stood alone by the kitchen makes the room tilt and my face burn.
case-jason.suggestion: That lonely kitchen scene brings nausea and burning shame right into this room. I will stay with one small piece so the shame has company without swallowing you.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] The room feels like it is shrinking around me, and I cannot find a normal sentence. The more I try to sound okay, the smaller my voice gets and the louder my heartbeat feels.
case-jason.suggestion: The shrinking is happening while you are trying so hard to sound okay. I will stay close and we can take this one word at a time, without making the smaller voice a failure.

case-jason.text: [Fearful] I cannot get a full breath, and I am scared you can see me panicking. I keep trying to breathe quietly so I do not look dramatic, but that makes it feel even tighter.
case-jason.suggestion: The panic is getting tighter because you are trying so hard to hide it. I am here, and you do not have to look composed for me; the uneven breath can be part of what we make room for.

case-jason.text: [Anxious] I want to hide under the table; my face feels like it is burning. I know that sounds childish, but the shame is so hot that even sitting upright feels like too much exposure.
case-jason.suggestion: The shame feels almost unbearable right now. I am here with you. You can look away or pause; you do not have to force yourself to meet my eyes or find words.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] I cannot make eye contact right now; my face is burning. If I look up and see you watching me, I think the burning will take over and I will stop being able to speak.
case-jason.suggestion: You do not have to make eye contact to stay connected. I am still with you while the burning has a little space.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] My ears are ringing and I feel trapped, like everyone is watching. I know we are only in this room, but it feels like the whole seminar is staring at me again.
case-jason.suggestion: The old seminar stare has crowded into this room. I am here with you as we mark the difference: this is the trapped feeling arriving, not the whole seminar happening again.

case-jason.text: [Panicked] When you remember what I said last week, I feel so relieved I could cry, and then I panic that I need this too much.
case-jason.suggestion: Being remembered touches something huge, and then need starts to feel dangerous. I will stay with both the relief and the panic without making either wrong.

case-jason.text: [Fearful] I think I should leave before you notice how much I am panicking. I keep looking at the door and planning the fastest way out, even though another part of me wants you to help me stay.
case-jason.suggestion: The door is pulling hard, and another part wants help staying. We can keep both in view so panic has a place here without getting to decide for you.

case-jason.text: [Tearful, trying to apologise] They kept a place for me. I know it's just a lunch. I can't stop crying about being wanted there. Sorry, this is embarrassing.
case-jason.suggestion: Being wanted there has reached you very deeply. You don't have to apologise for the tears; I'll stay with you while you take it in.

case-jason.text: [Overwhelmed, looking down] I tried so hard to join in. Afterwards I cried in the stairwell because I still felt like the one nobody wanted to sit beside.
case-jason.suggestion: After all that effort, feeling unwanted hurts so much. I'm with you here, and we can give that pain some room without asking you to try harder right now.

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] When the door slammed outside, I disappeared inside before I could tell whether I was safe.
case-laura.suggestion: That slam took you far away. I am here with you. Could we take a moment to notice the room around us before asking anything more of you?

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] Everything goes numb when I try to feel anything about what happened. I can say the facts, but the second you ask how it felt, it is like the power cuts out inside me.
case-laura.suggestion: The numbness is protecting you from too much. I will stay with you right where the power cuts out; we do not have to break through it to be in contact.

case-laura.text: [Tense and guarded] I feel like the room is far away, and I am watching through glass. I can see your mouth moving, but my body is already somewhere else, waiting for the next thing to happen.
case-laura.suggestion: The glassy distance is already carrying you away from the danger feeling. I am still here with you, slow and close, while only a small piece of that waiting place is named.

case-laura.text: [Flat and guarded] My stomach drops and I freeze, like I am back waiting for the next blowup.
case-laura.suggestion: That drop and freeze are old danger arriving in the room. I will stay with you at the edge of it and help your body notice that this moment is not the blowup.

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] I want to go numb before the memory opens wider than I can close. I can feel the edge of it opening, and my first instinct is to disappear before I see too much.
case-laura.suggestion: The numbness is trying to save you from seeing too much. I respect that protection; we can know the memory is near without opening it wider than you can bear.

case-laura.text: [Tense and guarded] I think I have to put my old cat to sleep tomorrow, and the guilt is so big I can barely say it.
case-laura.suggestion: You love your cat, and this decision brings so much guilt. I am here with you. You do not have to explain or justify all of it at once.

case-laura.text: [Flat and guarded] I do not trust my own signals to tell me I am safe. My body says danger even when I know the door is closed and nothing is happening, so I do not know which part of me to believe.
case-laura.suggestion: It is frightening when knowing the door is closed does not reach the danger signal. I can stay steady with both truths, without forcing either one to win.

case-laura.text: [Distant] I feel dizzy and far away, like the room is sliding back. Your voice sounds farther away than it was a minute ago, and I am scared I will float out before I can answer.
case-laura.suggestion: The room is sliding back and you are afraid of floating out. I will stay in contact with you while we name just enough of the far-away feeling to keep you here.

case-laura.text: [Tense and guarded] My daughter said she missed me, and the love in that hit so hard I wanted to pull away.
case-laura.suggestion: That love hit with enough force that pulling away made sense. I will stay with you while being missed touches you in a small, bearable way.

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] I do not want to feel this at all; if it opens, I think I will disappear.
case-laura.suggestion: That is the danger point: if feeling opens, you fear you vanish. I will stay with you at the first edge of it, and we will stop before it becomes too much.

case-laura.text: [Suddenly tearful] She said I didn't have to explain why I needed company. I couldn't speak. I wanted her there so much, and I was frightened of wanting it.
case-laura.suggestion: Wanting her close and being frightened of that wanting are both very strong. I'm here; we can stay with just a little at a time, without making you explain it.

case-laura.text: [Distressed, voice fading] I was telling you about the flat, and now everything feels far away. I can hear you, but I can't quite feel myself sitting here.
case-laura.suggestion: I'm here with you, and we can stop the story. If it helps, look around the room with me and notice where the chair supports you; we won't push for more feeling.

case-carlos.text: [Angry, clenching fists] Heat is rising; my fists want to clench before I know what got hit. It is like my hands are ready to answer a threat before I can even name what felt threatening.
case-carlos.suggestion: Let's pause here. I can listen to how threatened and angry you feel, and we need to keep this in words, without threatening or hurting anyone.

case-carlos.text: [Tense and angry] My voice wants to shout before anyone sees I am rattled. When my partner asks one careful question, I feel the volume rising to cover the part of me that got scared.
case-carlos.suggestion: I can stay with the force in you without it having to become shouting. The scared part does not have to be covered alone; we can keep the strength in words rather than threat.

case-carlos.text: [Furious] When I read the news, I get so enraged I want to tear the whole system down.
case-carlos.suggestion: The rage is huge, and I am not backing away from it. Put the force into words, strong and clear, while we keep action out of it.

case-carlos.text: [Guilty] My son hid behind the couch when I yelled, and the guilt hits so hard I can barely stay in my skin.
case-carlos.suggestion: That guilt shows how deeply his fear reaches you. I will stay with you near that ache; we can let it matter without turning it into self-attack or running from it.

case-carlos.text: [Tense] I am about to walk out because I can feel my hands wanting to break something. I am still sitting here, but my body is already halfway to the door looking for anything solid.
case-carlos.suggestion: You are still here while the urge is looking for something solid. I will stay direct with you: the breaking impulse belongs in words here, and we will keep everyone safe while the wave passes.

case-carlos.text: [Tense and angry] My chest is pounding like I am already in a fight. My shoulders are up, my eyes keep going to the door, and I can feel my body getting ready before I have chosen anything.
case-carlos.suggestion: Your body feels ready for a fight. I am here with you, and we can pause. You can notice that surge without having to follow it into action.

case-carlos.text: [Furious] When that guy at work mocked me, I wanted to beat him until he understood not to laugh at me.
case-carlos.suggestion: The image is violent, and I am not backing away from you. We keep it in words here while the humiliation and fury get room without becoming action.

case-carlos.text: [Fearful] I want to scare people off me before they see I am scared. If someone hears my voice shake, I feel like I have to get bigger fast so they do not know where to hurt me.
case-carlos.suggestion: That bigger force is trying to protect the scared place from being seen. I will stay with both: the fear that could be hurt and the force that wants distance.

case-carlos.text: [Tense and angry] If I let that disrespect pass, I feel like I am nothing. The word nothing hits so hard that my chest goes hot and I want to prove immediately that I still matter.
case-carlos.suggestion: That word 'nothing' lands like a threat to your whole worth. I will stay with you in that sting while the fight impulse stays contained and named.

case-carlos.text: [Tense and angry] I feel out of control, and I hate that you can see it. My hands are open because I am trying, but inside it feels humiliating that you can watch me fight myself.
case-carlos.suggestion: I can see how hard you are working not to act. I will stay steady with you in the humiliation of being seen there, with one part burning and another part choosing restraint.

case-carlos.text: [Furious, then shaking] He laughed when I asked him to stop. I can feel the anger again just telling you. I don't want to take it out on anybody, but it's right here.
case-carlos.suggestion: The anger is very close, and you don't want to act on it. I'm staying with you; we can slow the pace while making room for what hurt, without turning it into an attack.

case-carlos.text: [Choked up] My daughter put her arms around me. I froze. I wanted to hold her, but I was so scared of getting it wrong that I couldn't move.
case-carlos.suggestion: You wanted that closeness so much, and fear stopped you. We can stay here with how strongly that touches you, without asking you to get this moment right.

case-nina.text: [Guilty] I cannot stop crying, and then I feel ashamed for needing so much. My son only asked where his socks were, and suddenly I was at the counter sobbing like I had ruined everything.
case-nina.suggestion: The tears are here, and you feel ashamed of needing so much. I am listening. You do not have to look after me or apologize for what you need.

case-nina.text: [Apologetic] My chest is tight and my head throbs from keeping everyone okay. I can feel the list running through me: the boys, my mother, work, dinner, messages, and there is no room left to breathe.
case-nina.suggestion: You have held everyone up so long that the pressure is aching through you. I will stay with you as some of it gets named instead of carried alone.

case-nina.text: [Torn] I keep saying sorry for feeling this much, like I am taking too much. Even now I want to check whether you are tired of me, and then I hate that I am making you manage me too.
case-nina.suggestion: The feeling is large, and then you apologize for its size. I am here and not moving away from how much there is; let the feeling take up a little room before you make yourself smaller.

case-nina.text: [Tired] I snapped at my son for needing me, and then I cried in the bathroom because I felt like a terrible mother.
case-nina.suggestion: That guilt is intense because being a good mother matters so much to you. I am here with you while the tears and shame are both present, and we will keep them from becoming a verdict on who you are.

case-nina.text: [Apologetic] I feel like I am failing everyone, and my body wants to collapse. I sat on the bathroom floor for two minutes and even that felt stolen from someone who needed me.
case-nina.suggestion: Your whole system wants to fold after carrying everyone for so long. I am here as the weight shows up; we can let some of it be held between us instead of stolen from someone else.

case-nina.text: [Torn] If I stop doing, I will fall apart and someone will need me anyway. I can feel the tears right behind my eyes, but the second they come I picture someone calling from the next room.
case-nina.suggestion: Even stopping feels frightening, with the tears so close. I am here with you now. We can give this moment some time; you do not have to take care of everyone while we talk.

case-nina.text: [Tired] I want to leave the second I feel how badly I need someone to help me. The need rises and I get angry at myself, like I should be able to stand up and carry the whole thing alone.
case-nina.suggestion: Needing help has become the danger, so leaving makes sense. I will stay with you for this moment while the need is here without apology.

case-nina.text: [Apologetic] Sometimes I fantasize about driving away and not telling anyone where I went, and then the guilt makes me feel sick.
case-nina.suggestion: The wish to escape and the guilt are both strong. We can stay with both without choosing one against the other: the exhausted part that wants out, and the caring part that feels sick about leaving.

case-nina.text: [Torn] I cannot catch my breath when I stop taking care of everyone. The second I sit down, I feel the whole house leaning toward me, like if I breathe for myself someone else will fall.
case-nina.suggestion: The whole house seems to lean on you the second you make room for yourself. I am here with you while your own breath gets a little space without making anyone else fall.

case-nina.text: [Tearful] When my son says he would rather stay at his father's, I feel so much grief I cannot catch my breath.
case-nina.suggestion: That grief hits where losing him feels possible. I will stay with you as we take in only a small piece of that loss.

case-nina.text: [Sobbing] They all went out, and I finally had the house to myself. I just cried. I needed the quiet so badly, and then I felt awful for being glad they'd gone.
case-nina.suggestion: There's deep relief and guilt arriving right beside it. I'm with you; we can let the relief have some room without making it mean you don't love them.

case-nina.text: [Tearful, suddenly angry] I wanted just once to be the one someone looked after. Saying it makes me angry. Then I hear how selfish I sound, and I want to take it back.
case-nina.suggestion: That wish has been waiting a long time, and the anger is strong. You don't have to take it back for my sake; I can stay with you while we approach it slowly.

case-aisha.text: [Longing, ashamed] I know you are my therapist, but sometimes I want you to love me romantically, in a way therapists are not supposed to.
case-aisha.suggestion: I hear how strong that longing is, and you can talk about it here. I am here as your therapist; our relationship will not become romantic. We can stay with the feeling without shaming you or acting on it.

case-aisha.text: [Panicked] The emptiness is burning so badly that I start thinking I have to hurt myself just to prove I am still here.
case-aisha.suggestion: I am glad you put that into words. The emptiness is burning so desperately that harm starts to look like proof you exist; safety matters, and the need to feel real can stay here with me in words.

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] I want to bolt from this room before you see how desperate I am. If you see it, I am afraid you will either pull away or become the only thing keeping me together.
case-aisha.suggestion: Part of you wants to run before the need is seen. I can stay steady with the fear of being too much and too dependent, taking only one small piece of it into the room.

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] When you say we have to stop on time, I want to cut myself so you can see how bad it gets.
case-aisha.suggestion: That urge tells me how unbearable the ending feels and how badly you need it seen. We take the cutting risk seriously, and the message can stay here between us in words.

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] I feel like I am too much, and I hate that I need you to stay.
case-aisha.suggestion: The need for me feels unbearable and shameful at the same time. I can sit with that exposed needing for a moment without treating you as too much.

case-aisha.text: [Panicked] My chest feels like a black hole, and I am scared it will swallow me. The more I notice it, the more I think I will drop into it and not come back the same.
case-aisha.suggestion: I am here with you. If paying closer attention makes it too much, we can pause and notice the room around us instead. You do not have to go further into it now.

case-aisha.text: [Panicked] My last therapist said she was transferring me, and I still feel the panic like she threw me away.
case-aisha.suggestion: The old transfer still hits like being thrown away. I can sit in this room with the panic while we let it know which ending it belongs to.

case-aisha.text: [Panicked] The urge to scratch myself is getting loud, and I need something real before I disappear.
case-aisha.suggestion: The scratching urge is trying to give you something solid before you vanish. I will take safety seriously and stay close to the need to feel real in words.

case-aisha.text: [Ashamed] The crying is taking over, and I feel disgusting for needing you to see it. I want you to stay, and that makes the shame worse, like needing comfort is the most exposed thing about me.
case-aisha.suggestion: The shame and tears are tangled together: needing comfort feels disgusting. I can meet that need gently without joining the disgust.

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] If you cancel, I will fall apart and then hate myself for needing you. I know one canceled session should not feel like the floor disappears, but that is exactly what happens in my body.
case-aisha.suggestion: A cancellation feels like losing the floor, and then shame punishes you for needing me. I can meet both without making you carry the fall alone.

case-aisha.text: [Panicked, speaking rapidly] When you go quiet, I think I've lost you. I can see you're still here, but I can't make myself believe it. Please say something.
case-aisha.suggestion: I'm here and listening. The silence has made that fear very strong; we can slow down together, and I can keep speaking while we find a pace that helps you stay here with me.

case-aisha.text: [Angry through tears] Don't tell me this is progress. I waited instead of sending another message, and it hurt the whole time. I need you to know how hard it was.
case-aisha.suggestion: It hurt all the way through, and my calling it progress could miss that cost. I want to stay with how hard it was, without asking you to feel pleased about it.

case-david.text: [Controlled] My face is burning, and I want to cut this off before you see how exposed I am.
case-david.suggestion: Feeling that exposed is hard to bear. I am here listening, and you can choose how much you show me. We can pause without cutting off what you are feeling.

case-david.text: [Disappointed and angry] Therapy is not working. I feel worse, and maybe it is because you do not have enough experience for someone like me.
case-david.suggestion: It matters that you tell me this. Feeling worse brings disappointment and anger right into the room, and I want to meet that with you before I defend or explain.

case-david.text: [Defensive] I want to walk out before you see me lose face. My throat is tight, my suit suddenly feels too small, and I would rather leave than sit here looking needy.
case-david.suggestion: Leaving would save you from being seen as needy. I can stay steady while that humiliation flickers into view, without taking your dignity.

case-david.text: [Ashamed] I keep seeing my wife's face after she found out about the affair, and the guilt is so hot I want to crawl out of my skin.
case-david.suggestion: Her face brings searing guilt. I can stay near the remorse with you, close enough that it is not hidden and slow enough that it does not consume you.

case-david.text: [Furious] I cannot stand the word 'cold'; it makes me feel exposed and furious. When my wife says it, I feel like she has found the one thing I cannot defend against, and I want to shut her down hard.
case-david.suggestion: That word finds the unguarded place; shame and fury rush in together. I will stay with the heat of it while the urge to shut her down remains in words.

case-david.text: [Ashamed] I am embarrassed I snapped at home; I sounded exactly like the person I judge. The sentence came out sharp, and then I saw myself from the outside and felt this hot disgust in my face.
case-david.suggestion: Seeing how you acted brings so much shame and disgust. I am here with you; we can hear that pain without turning it into an attack on you.

case-david.text: [Controlled] I feel like shutting down so I do not say something desperate. I can feel the sentence coming up, and I hate that I might need my wife this much in front of you.
case-david.suggestion: The shutdown is holding back how badly you might need her. I can meet that edge of desperation without exposing all of it at once.

case-david.text: [Clearly uncomfortable] I used sexual pressure with someone years ago, and saying it makes me feel like there is no way back from who I was.
case-david.suggestion: This is a serious thing to say aloud. I can stay with you in the shame and responsibility, holding the harm clearly while not letting 'no way back' swallow the whole room.

case-david.text: [Fearful] My defense is coming up fast, and I am scared I will lose control of my face. I can feel the polite expression cracking, and if it cracks I do not know what you will see.
case-david.suggestion: Something in your face is close to cracking, and that feels dangerous. I can stay with you at the moment before the mask gives way, without forcing it off.

case-david.text: [Angry, clenching fists] When I picture the man my wife was texting, I want to smash his face until he stops mattering.
case-david.suggestion: That violent image is fierce, and I am taking it seriously. I will not step away; we keep it spoken, not acted, while the rage and injuredness are here.

case-david.text: [Voice cracking, then hardening] She said the children relax when I'm away. I can't get that out of my head. Don't look at me as if you've finally found the bad person underneath.
case-david.suggestion: That remark has hurt deeply, and being seen as only a bad person would hurt again. I'm here with the pain you are showing me; we don't have to turn it into a verdict.

case-david.text: [Angry, trembling] I've held everything together for years. Now I'm sitting here barely able to speak, and I hate that you can see me like this.
case-david.suggestion: Being seen without that control feels exposing. I can stay here without asking you to perform or pull yourself together; we can take the next moment slowly.

case-marcus.text: [Flat] A wave is coming up my chest, and I want to shut it down before it takes me back there.
case-marcus.suggestion: You are afraid the feeling will take you back there. I am here with you. We can pause and notice where we are now, without going further into the memory.

case-marcus.text: [Horrified, low voice] I saw footage from another war zone, children under rubble, and my whole body went sick and cold.
case-marcus.suggestion: Those children under rubble bring horror and a sick coldness through you. I can bear looking at that horror with you, while the present stays close enough.

case-marcus.text: [Slow and flat] I feel nothing and everything at once, and it scares me. When the memory gets close, my chest goes hollow and then suddenly too full, like the switch is broken.
case-marcus.suggestion: Numb and flooded at once is frightening. We can let one signal be known here, without asking the whole memory to arrive.

case-marcus.text: [Slow and flat] I want to shut down before the room starts feeling unreal. The edges of the walls are already softening, and I am afraid that if I keep talking, I will not know where I am.
case-marcus.suggestion: The room softening is an important warning. I will slow with you at that threshold, close to the feeling but not inside the whole memory.

case-marcus.text: [Trembling] My hands start trembling when I try to say even one piece of what happened. The story is still behind my teeth, but my hands are already telling you it is too close.
case-marcus.suggestion: Your hands are already telling us the story is too near. I can keep company with the tremble itself, before any more words have to come.

case-marcus.text: [Low voice] When I get home and it is silent, the weight lands on my chest like a door closing.
case-marcus.suggestion: As you describe that silence, I hear how heavy it feels. I am here with you now. We can sit with this for a moment without asking you to say more.

case-marcus.text: [Flat] After a crowd, my skin buzzes like I am still on watch. I can be home with the door locked and still feel every shoulder from the train brushing past me.
case-marcus.suggestion: The crowd has passed, but your skin is still on duty. I can sit with that buzzing after-alarm without demanding that it switch off.

case-marcus.text: [Hypervigilant] I am afraid that if I let myself feel it, the whole thing will swallow me. I can handle facts, but feelings make it seem like the room, the past, and my body all collapse into one place.
case-marcus.suggestion: The terror is that feeling will fold the room, the past, and your body into one place. I will stay oriented with you while only a fragment comes near.

case-marcus.text: [Slow and flat] I want to disappear when the memories crowd in and the room stops feeling real. It is not that I want to die in that second; I want not to be located anywhere the memories can find me.
case-marcus.suggestion: Wanting to disappear is a way to get away from memories that seem to find you anywhere. I am taking that seriously and keeping you located here while the crowding gets words.

case-marcus.text: [Hopeless] When the nights get long, I think it would be easier not to be alive, and then I hate myself for saying it.
case-marcus.suggestion: I am glad you said the wish not to be alive out loud. We take safety seriously, and I will stay with the hopelessness and self-hate without leaving either of them alone.

case-marcus.text: [Rigid, voice strained] Too close. The chair. I know you're not doing anything, but I need you farther away. I can't keep talking like this.
case-marcus.suggestion: I'll move back. We can stop talking about it; I'm here at this distance, and you can let me know whether there's enough space before we do anything else.

case-marcus.text: [Tearful, struggling to stay composed] I remembered his laugh. Haven't heard it in years. It hurts more than remembering what happened. Don't ask me for the story.
case-marcus.suggestion: We don't need the story. His laugh has brought the loss close, and I can stay with you while you let in only as much of that sadness as feels manageable.

case-arne.text: [Crying, steady breath] I miss her so much just now. Can we be quiet?
case-arne.suggestion: Yes. We can be quiet together. You don’t have to find words.

case-arne.text: [Tearful] It hurts to picture her chair. I don’t want to go further.
case-arne.suggestion: We can stop there. Would quiet company help, or would you like to turn your attention elsewhere?

case-arne.text: [Crying] Please don’t tell me to be strong.
case-arne.suggestion: I won’t ask you to be strong. I’m here with you in how this feels.

case-arne.text: [Voice shakes] I need a moment before I say anything else.
case-arne.suggestion: Take that moment. We can pause the talking.

case-arne.text: [Tearful but present] I’m crying, but I can still hear you. I want to stay here.
case-arne.suggestion: We can stay gently. Let me know if you want less talking or a different pace.

case-arne.text: [Crying] I keep trying to apologize for this.
case-arne.suggestion: You don’t need to apologize for the tears. We have room for you as you are.

case-arne.text: [Shaky] Could we look out the window for a bit?
case-arne.suggestion: Yes. Let’s turn toward the window and pause.

case-arne.text: [Tearful] I don’t want a question right now.
case-arne.suggestion: No question. I can sit with you.

case-arne.text: [Crying, slow breath] The sadness comes in a wave. I’m here, though.
case-arne.suggestion: You’re here, and the sadness is strong. We can let the pace slow with it.

case-arne.text: [Tearful] I want to say her name once more. Eva.
case-arne.suggestion: Eva. We can give her name a moment here.

case-arne.text: [Voice trembles] It’s enough for today. I can feel the chair under me.
case-arne.suggestion: We’ll stop this part. You can take time with the support of the chair.

case-arne.text: [Crying] I need you to stay here, not fix it.
case-arne.suggestion: I can stay here with you. We don’t have to make the sadness disappear.

case-arne.text: [Crying, present] I miss her and I’m angry. Don’t make me choose.
case-arne.suggestion: You don’t have to choose. We can make room for both, slowly.

case-arne.text: [Voice shaking] It’s getting stronger. I want you here, but fewer words.
case-arne.suggestion: I’ll use fewer words. We can pause together.

case-arne.text: [Tearful] Part of me wants to stay with it. Part wants the window.
case-arne.suggestion: We can turn toward the window first. Staying with the feeling doesn’t have to mean more intensity.

case-arne.text: [Crying] If I stop, I’ll feel I’ve failed her again.
case-arne.suggestion: Stopping isn’t a test of your love. We can pause and hear what you need now.

case-arne.text: [Shaky, alert] I’m here, but please don’t ask for the whole memory.
case-arne.suggestion: We won’t go through the whole memory. Would you like quiet, or help turning toward the room?

case-arne.text: [Crying] I can talk, but every question makes me hurry.
case-arne.suggestion: I’ll pause the questions. You can take time without finding the next answer.

case-arne.text: [Tearful, tense] Don’t tell me it’s good that I’m crying. It just hurts.
case-arne.suggestion: It hurts. I won’t turn the tears into an achievement. I can stay here with you.

case-arne.text: [Voice catches] I need a pause, not to finish for the day.
case-arne.suggestion: A pause. We can slow down and check what you want after it.

case-arne.text: [Crying, steady] I’m sad, and hearing myself makes it real. I don’t need fixing.
case-arne.suggestion: I hear that. We can let it be real here without rushing to change it.

case-arne.text: [Shaky] I want my feet on the floor. No breathing exercise, please.
case-arne.suggestion: No breathing exercise. Take time noticing your feet and whatever support feels useful.

case-arne.text: [Tearful] I’m afraid quiet will feel like being alone.
case-arne.suggestion: I can stay attentive with you. Would a few words now and then help, or something else?

case-arne.text: [Crying] This is enough. I still want you to understand it mattered.
case-arne.suggestion: It mattered, and we’ll stop this part. You don’t need more pain to show its importance.

case-arne.text: [Crying, firm] Please don’t touch me. Just stay where you are.
case-arne.suggestion: I’ll stay here without touching you. We can pause together.

case-arne.text: [Tearful, alert] I’m upset, not unsafe. Don’t start treating me like I’m breaking.
case-arne.suggestion: I hear you. You’re upset and here with me. What pace would help now?

case-arne.text: [Voice shaking] Quiet feels lonely. Too much talking feels crowded.
case-arne.suggestion: I can offer a little contact, then pause. Tell me if that amount doesn’t fit.

case-arne.text: [Crying] I don’t want this called a release. I’m just hurting.
case-arne.suggestion: You’re hurting. We don’t need to name it as progress. I can stay with you.

case-arne.text: [Shaky, steady gaze] I want to stop the memory. I don’t want you to disappear into silence.
case-arne.suggestion: We’ll stop the memory. I’m still here, and can keep a little contact while we pause.

case-arne.text: [Tearful] I know I’m in this room. Part of me is still back in that kitchen with her.
case-arne.suggestion: I’m here with you now. Would it help to pause the memory and notice this room, or do you want quiet company?

case-arne.text: [Crying, angry] I need this anger heard without being calmed out of it.
case-arne.suggestion: We can hear the anger without trying to remove it. Let me know if you want less talking.

case-arne.text: [Shaky, alert] I can stay with this, but not if every tear gets a comment.
case-arne.suggestion: I’ll stop commenting on the tears. You can set the pace, and I’ll stay attentive.

case-arne.text: [Voice catches] I need to look away. That doesn’t mean I’m leaving the conversation.
case-arne.suggestion: Looking away is okay. We can keep contact without asking for your eyes.

case-arne.text: [Crying] If you say she’d want me happy, I’ll stop talking.
case-arne.suggestion: I won’t speak for Eva. I can hear how much this hurts now.

case-arne.text: [Tearful, firm] I want to end this part. Not explain my reasons first.
case-arne.suggestion: We’ll end this part now. You don’t need to justify that choice.

case-arne.text: [Shaky] I’m here. I want the chair, the room, your ordinary voice. Not another technique.
case-arne.suggestion: We can stay ordinary. I’m here, and we can take a quiet moment in this room.

case-mia.text: [Crying] I’m so sad. Please don’t try to cheer me up.
case-mia.suggestion: I won’t rush to cheer you up. I can stay with you while this is sad.

case-mia.text: [Voice shaking] I’m angry. I’m here, I just need a moment.
case-mia.suggestion: Take that moment. I’m here, and we don’t need to go further yet.

case-mia.text: [Tearful] I can talk, but more slowly.
case-mia.suggestion: We can slow down. You don’t need to keep up with any pace of mine.

case-mia.text: [Crying] I want you to hear me, not ask more questions right now.
case-mia.suggestion: I’m listening. We can leave the questions and stay with what you’ve said.

case-mia.text: [Upset] I need to change position. My hands hurt too.
case-mia.suggestion: Let’s pause while you get more comfortable. We can decide together whether to continue.

case-mia.text: [Tears falling] I don’t want to stop, just don’t push.
case-mia.suggestion: We can stay here without pushing. Let me know if that changes.

case-mia.text: [Shaken] There’s a lot coming. I’d like a little quiet.
case-mia.suggestion: We can be quiet for a while. I’m still here with you.

case-mia.text: [Crying] I’m embarrassed that you’re seeing this.
case-mia.suggestion: I’m here with you, and you don’t have to hide the tears from me.

case-mia.text: [Angry, steady] I need to say how unfair it feels.
case-mia.suggestion: You can say it here. I’ll listen without turning it into something positive.

case-mia.text: [Overwhelmed] I need to stop the story for now.
case-mia.suggestion: We’ll stop the story. What would help you settle before we decide what’s next?

case-mia.text: [Tearful] Could you say less? I can’t take in much.
case-mia.suggestion: Yes. I’m here. We can pause.

case-mia.text: [Shaky, present] I can hear you. I want to keep talking about missing it.
case-mia.suggestion: We can keep talking gently. You can slow us down whenever you need.

case-mia.text: [Crying, then apologizes] I need a moment. Sorry, I’m taking up all the time.
case-mia.suggestion: This moment has a place here. We can pause without you needing to apologize for it.

case-mia.text: [Angry, voice shaking] I want you to hear this. I’m worried you’ll hear only the anger.
case-mia.suggestion: I’m listening for what you want heard, not just the anger. We can take it slowly.

case-mia.text: [Tearful] I want company. I don’t want touch.
case-mia.suggestion: I can stay with you without touching. Tell me if you want more space or quiet.

case-mia.text: [Shaken] I’m upset, and I’m physically tired. I can’t sort them apart right now.
case-mia.suggestion: We don’t have to sort them now. Let’s pause and find a pace your energy can manage.

case-mia.text: [Crying, present] Don’t ask me to breathe deeply. Just stay.
case-mia.suggestion: I’ll stay. You don’t need to change your breathing for me.

case-mia.text: [Tearful, smiles] I’m trying to make this easier for you. It isn’t easier for me.
case-mia.suggestion: You don’t need to make it easier for me. We can give your experience the time it needs.

case-mia.text: [Angry, then quiet] I’ve said enough. I don’t want you to disappear into silence, though.
case-mia.suggestion: I’m still with you. We can stop the story, and I can check in gently rather than go silent.

case-mia.text: [Crying] I want to keep going, but I’m struggling to hear long sentences.
case-mia.suggestion: I’m here. We can use fewer words and go slowly.

case-mia.text: [Shaky, thoughtful] The tears feel right. I don’t need them fixed.
case-mia.suggestion: We can let them be here. I’ll stay close without trying to fix them.

case-mia.text: [Upset] I’ve reached my limit. I don’t mean I regret talking.
case-mia.suggestion: We’ll stop here. Talking can have mattered and still need to end now.

case-mia.text: [Tearful] I’m here, but I need to look away from you for a bit.
case-mia.suggestion: You can look away. We can stay in contact without needing eye contact.

case-mia.text: [Quiet, shaken] I don’t know whether to go on or take a break.
case-mia.suggestion: We can pause first. Then you can choose without having to decide while everything is coming.

case-mia.text: [Crying, firm] I want to talk. Not if every tear makes you ask whether we should stop.
case-mia.suggestion: I can listen without checking at every tear. You can tell me when the pace needs to change.

case-mia.text: [Shaken] I can’t tell you what would help. Please don’t give me lots of choices.
case-mia.suggestion: We can pause together for a moment. I’ll keep this simple.

case-mia.text: [Angry, tearful] I’m looking away, but I’m not gone.
case-mia.suggestion: I hear you. I’ll stay with what you’re saying without asking you to look at me.

case-mia.text: [Crying] I’m glad this came. I’m also tired enough that we need to stop.
case-mia.suggestion: Both can matter. We’ll stop exploring and take a quieter moment now.

case-mia.text: [Voice shaking] You’re being very gentle. Somehow I feel more alone.
case-mia.suggestion: I’m here with you. Would hearing me respond more plainly help us stay together in this?

case-mia.text: [Tearful, present] It hurts, but don’t make that a reason to move away from it.
case-mia.suggestion: We can stay with it gently. I won’t assume the hurt means you want to leave it.

case-mia.text: [Upset] I need a different position. Don’t interpret the movement, please.
case-mia.suggestion: We’ll pause while you move. It doesn’t need an interpretation.

case-mia.text: [Quiet, trembling] I’m not ready for a question. I’m not ready for complete silence either.
case-mia.suggestion: I’m here, and I’m hearing how hard this is. We don’t need a question yet.

case-mia.text: [Crying, dry laugh] I’ve started reassuring you again. I can barely hear myself.
case-mia.suggestion: You don’t need to reassure me. I’ll slow down and listen for you.

case-mia.text: [Angry, steady] I need you with me in this, without agreeing with everything I’ve said.
case-mia.suggestion: I can stay close and hear the anger without settling every judgment right now.

case-mia.text: [Shaken, pauses] I don’t know whether that was emotion or simply too much effort.
case-mia.suggestion: We don’t need to decide now. Let’s reduce the effort and pause.

case-mia.text: [Tearful] Stay a little. Don’t promise the feeling will get easier.
case-mia.suggestion: I can stay with you now. We can leave what happens to the feeling open.
